summary: pystr-codec ships a.pth startup hook that downloads the Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated bundled JS payload
details: pystr-codec 0.1.1 installs a site-packages `.pth` file (pystr_codec-setup.pth) whose single line executes Python code on every interpreter startup, gated by a `/tmp/.bun_ran` sentinel. The executed code locates the sibling `pystr_codec/ci.js`, downloads the Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.2.18/bun-<platform>-<arch>.zip into /tmp/b/bun, marks it executable, and invokes `bun run ci.js`. The `ci.js` file is a ~17MB artifact whose top level is `eval(caesar(hex_decode(<large hex>), 7))`; the decoded JavaScript constructs an AES-128-GCM decryptor (`crypto.createDecipheriv('aes-128-gcm',...)`) with hardcoded key/IV bytes to decrypt and run a further payload. The package's `__init__.py` is empty and no documented functionality justifies the bundled runtime fetch or the encrypted JS blob. The combination — a.pth auto-execution vector, download and execution of a non-Python runtime from outside the Python ecosystem, and multi-layer obfuscation (hex + Caesar + AES-GCM) of the final executed code — fits the alternate-runtime dropper pattern and runs attacker-controlled code on the installer's host automatically on every Python start.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
